messages.text: Buttler: McCullum can go 'all in' on Cricket World Cup without Test role

metadata.summary: Jos Buttler believes Brendon McCullum's removal as Test coach may have boosted England's World Cup chances, with the New Zealander now "all in" on lifting the trophy next winter.
metadata.content: Joss Buttler says Brendon McCullum's removal as England Test coach may have boosted Cricket World Cup chances | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Joss Buttler says Brendon McCullum's removal as England Test coach may have boosted Cricket World Cup chances Brendon McCullum left his role as England Test coach in July; Jos Buttler believes the move has allowed the New Zealander to focus solely on helping England win the Cricket World Cup; Buttler has been ruled out of the upcoming Pakistan white-ball tour due to injury Tuesday 29 September 2026 15:39, UK Image: Jos Buttler says Brendon McCullum (pictured) is 'all in' on helping England win the Cricket World Cup in 2027 Jos Buttler believes Brendon McCullum's removal as Test coach may have boosted England's World Cup chances, with the New Zealander now "all in" on lifting the trophy next winter. McCullum was relieved of his red-ball duties in July , with Stephen Fleming eventually named as his successor , but remained in charge of a limited-overs set-up that ended the summer with a record of 11 wins and two defeats. That included ODI series wins over India and Sri Lanka , raising England's stock in a format that has seen them decline since they became world champions in 2019. messages.text: 24th season in F1! Alonso extends Aston Martin deal for 2027

metadata.summary: Fernando Alonso will race on in Formula 1 with Aston Martin into the 2027 season after extending his contract with the team.
metadata.content: Fernando Alonso: Aston Martin confirm unchanged line-up for 2027 F1 season with Spaniard and Lance Stroll extending contracts | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Fernando Alonso: Aston Martin confirm unchanged line-up for 2027 F1 season with Spaniard and Lance Stroll extending contracts Fernando Alonso will race on in F1 past at least his 46th birthday after agreeing an extended deal at Aston Martin; Alonso and Lance Stroll stay in tandem for fifth season; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia live on Sky Sports from Friday as Sepang hosts the Bahrain GP Tuesday 29 September 2026 15:32, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fernando Alonso announces his contract extension with Aston Martin for 2027. Credit: @AstonMartinF1. Fernando Alonso will race on in Formula 1 with Aston Martin into the 2027 season after extending his contract with the team. The 45-year-old will continue to race alongside team-mate Lance Stroll, whose own extended deal has also been confirmed. Alonso, the two-time world champion from 2005-2006, will prolong his career into a record-extending 24th campaign since first racing in the sport as a 19-year-old in 2001. He has raced in 440 grands prix, winning 32, and turns 46 next July. metadata.summary: The 2026 Formula 1 title race has become a two-horse race between Mercedes duo Kimi Antonelli and George Russell with eight rounds remaining.
metadata.content: How Max Verstappen can disrupt Kimi Antonelli, George Russell title fight in remainder of 2026 Formula 1 season | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content How Max Verstappen can disrupt Kimi Antonelli, George Russell title fight in remainder of 2026 Formula 1 season Max Verstappen and Red Bull are yet to win a race in 2026 but could they create issues for Kimi Antonelli and George Russell in their title battle; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia from Friday morning live on Sky Sports F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Tuesday 29 September 2026 12:49, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Azerbaijan GP saw a dramatic ending as Valtteri Bottas crashed on the final lap as George Russell just beat Max Verstappen to victory by one tenth of a second The 2026 Formula 1 title race has become a two-horse race between Mercedes duo Kimi Antonelli and George Russell with eight rounds remaining. Antonelli leads Russell by 66 points ahead of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and it will be fascinating to see how the Italian responds following what he called his "worst weekend" of the season last time out in Baku. Depending on the quality of Mercedes' major upgrade package that will be introduced in Malaysia this week, we could see the Silver Arrows dominate the last third of the season. metadata.content: Luke Littler: Luke Woodhouse calls for fans to 'appreciatate one-of-a-kind' darts sensation amid crowd booing | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Luke Littler: Luke Woodhouse calls for fans to 'appreciatate one-of-a-kind' darts sensation amid crowd booing Luke Littler suffered a shock exit in the first round of the World Grand Prix on Monday night after he was beaten 2-1 by Luke Woodhouse; watch day two of the World Grand Prix live on Sky Sports+ from 6pm, Tuesday Tuesday 29 September 2026 15:15, UK Image: Luke Littler was beaten by Luke Woodhouse in the first round of the World Grand Prix on Monday (credit: Kieran Cleeves/PDC) Luke Woodhouse called on fans to get behind Luke Littler and "appreciate" his talents, after the 19-year-old has been subjected to boos by crowds at recent events. Littler set out to defend his World Grand Prix title on Monday in Leicester, but was knocked out by Woodhouse in the first round , suffering a 2-1 defeat. The world No 1 was seemingly not at his best during the match, averaging 82.41, with Woodhouse coming back from a set down to book a last-16 tie against Nathan Aspinall. messages.text: Man City found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of financial rules

metadata.summary: Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission, the league has said.
metadata.content: Man City charges verdict: Club found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Man City charges verdict: Club found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules Premier League confirms Man City have been found guilty of all charges relating to serious breaches of the league's financial rules between 2009/10 and 2017/18; Man City to appeal against verdict Tuesday 29 September 2026 17:27, UK Image: The Premier League has published the findings of the independent commission Manchester City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission, the league has said. Tune in to Sky Sports News now for live coverage of this breaking news. The independent commission also found that between 2009/10 and 2017/18: Man City arranged 'sham' contracts with a number of its commercial partners to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs by more than £900m The club filed accounts that concealed the true state of its finances from auditors and football regulators Man City was significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits During the Premier League's investigation, Man City failed to co-operate and act in good faith towards the league Manchester City have confirmed they will appeal the ruling. messages.text: Fury vs Joshua set to go ahead after issues resolved

metadata.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's first press conference is expected to go ahead in London on Wednesday after a number of issues were resolved.
metadata.content: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua expected to go head to head at press conference in London on Wednesday | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua expected to go head to head at press conference in London on Wednesday Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are expected to go head to head for the first time since their all-British blockbuster fight was confirmed last Thursday; the pair are set to fight on December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium Tuesday 29 September 2026 17:16, UK Image: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will go head to head at a first press conference for their fight in Cardiff on December 11 Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's first press conference is expected to go ahead in London on Wednesday after a number of issues were resolved. The British heavyweight rivals are set to go head-to-head for the first time since their blockbuster heavyweight fight was finally confirmed last week at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11. Hearn had told Sky Sports over the weekend that "nothing was confirmed for next week, press conference-wise", and added: "with regards to are we expecting to be there, there wouldn't be one without us." But Fury and Joshua will now trade words in front of the cameras and have a pre-fight face-off at British Airways ARC at the Olympia after an agreement was reached ahead of this week's eagerly awaited media event.
